description: The jury in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of murder after strangling her three young children, has asked to review her prescription pill bottles and a kitchen knife, according to defense attorney Kevin Reddington. Clancy was prescribed about a dozen medications as her mental health declined in the months before the January 2023 killings. Clancy has pleaded not guilty to three counts of murder and faces life in prison if convicted. CNN's Jean Casarez reports from Plymouth, Massachusetts.

description:
As the Trump administration ratchets up efforts to deport non-citizens from the US, people with papers they thought allowed them to be in the country are being targeted.

Also, ICE arrests have soared as the agency is edging closer to its goal of 2,000 arrests a day. New data shows that a majority of the people arrested by ICE in July have no criminal convictions or have been charged with a crime. Abby Phillip's "NewsNight" panel debates whether ICE should target those without criminal records.

0:00 "Chaos": Trump admin ratchets up immigration ops at airports
1:13 "You may remain in the US until your asylum application is decided," but she was arrested anyway
6:02 New data shows majority of ICE arrestees don't have criminal convictions or charges
8:13 "That seems like a bit of a bait-and-switch" when ICE targets those using legal pathways
9:36 Is ICE really going after "the worst of the worst", as the administration has claimed?

Watch 24/7 live news with CNN Headlines: https://bit.l
title: 'Worst of the worst'? ICE arrests soar as agency targets asylum seekers

author: CNN
description:
In their latest update, the country’s national disaster agency said that 579 people had died, with 1,924 people missing, including 517 foreign nationals.

Nepal and China have restarted rescue operations in areas devastated by flash flooding, after a pause sparked by fears a barrier lake could unleash another deluge. China’s first professional rescue team finally reached Gyirong port, the area most affected by catastrophic landslides — which have been described as “liquid concrete.”

An Indian-American couple who survived the flood have recounted how they narrowly managed to escape to higher ground and were eventually airlifted to safety by the Nepali army.

2:00 Couple recounts their survival after the deadly floods
4:00 Daughters on the hopes to find their missing parents

#News
title: Survivors describe China-Nepal flash flood as 570+ dead, 1900+ missing

description: The flooding in Nepal is hitting close to home for a longtime member of the CNN family.
